newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Netherlands to host conference on ACP relations.
newsitem.headline: Netherlands to host conference on ACP relations.

text.p: The Dutch EU presidency will host a conference early next year aimed at defining the future of the Union's relations with the African, Caribbean and Pacific group of developing countries.

The Hague announced the plan at a meeting of the Development Council at which ministers discussed for the first time a European Commission discussion paper drafted ahead of the expiry of the current Lome aid and trade pact in February 2000.
In the paper the Commission noted that despite 40 years of European Union assistance, 41 out of the 50 poorest countries of the world were ACP states.
The meeting in the Netherlands will bring together EU member states, non-governmental organisations working in development and representatives from the ACP states themselves.
The Commission notes that the countries' participation in international trade remains marginal and prospects of escaping from poverty are extremely worrying.
Many ministers at Friday's development ministers meeting said that the exhaustive study was so bulky that it was not user-friendly.
The Commission plans to present proposals to the Council of Ministers in the second half of 1997 and start negotiations for a new pact with the 70 ACP states in September 1998.
